steps.what: Show the amount due for the accepted transportation and accommodations.
Collect payment for transportation and accommodations from the customer.
Record the payment the agent collected.

tasks.design: The amount due for transportation and accommodations is shown from the accepted quote in {CRM}. The travel agent collects that payment from the customer. The payment record stores the amount and a reference, not the full card number. An amount with no quote id is not shown. The screen does not take the payment.
tasks.previous_blocker: The amount was read from a handwritten total, and the record was typed again afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: An accepted quote can show the amount. The agent still collects it.
tasks.still_hard: Taking the payment, and seeing that the customer agrees the amount, is the agent's work.
tasks.human_edge: The agent collects the payment. A shown amount is not the collection.
tasks.altitude: Collection stays with the agent. The record files only the payment the agent collected against the accepted quote.

reach.task: Collect a payment the buyer has agreed.
reach.learn: A shown amount is not the taking of the money.

evidence.claim: A quote the agent has already accepted can show the amount due. It cannot collect the money.
The payment record should keep the amount and a reference. It should not keep the full card number.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A travel agent in a mid-size European company. A tariff line is not a trip, and a draft is not a booking.
Fields: A quote id and an amount are required. With no quote id, the agent collects from the paper total. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the travel agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The record stores the amount and a payment reference. It does not store the full card number.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the travel agent.
unknowns: Whether payment is taken in the shop or by a link the customer opens.
research_questions: Which payments are still written in a day book and typed into the client record later?

already_counted.description: Collecting the payment from the customer stays with the agent.

incremental.description: Check the amount on screen is the quote the customer agreed.

approvals.approved_version: payment version and the quote id it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes the quote has no id, so the agent reads the amount from paper and the collection is unchanged. High assumes the accepted amount is shown. Taking the payment stays with the agent.

steps.what: List various itinerary packages and promotional travel incentives offered.
Plan, describe, arrange, and sell those packages to the customer.
File the package the customer chose from those carriers.

tasks.design: Itinerary packages and promotional travel incentives that carriers have already offered are listed from {CRM}. The travel agent plans, describes, arranges, and sells. The chosen package is filed only after the agent accepts it. A package with no id is not listed. The list does not sell the trip.
tasks.previous_blocker: Carrier offers sat in separate brochures, so the agent rebuilt the list in the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Offers the company already holds can be listed. The agent still sells.
tasks.still_hard: Which package fits this customer is a conversation, not a sort of incentives.
tasks.human_edge: The agent describes the trip and sells it. A list of offers does not.
tasks.altitude: The sale stays with the agent. The file holds only the package the customer chose and the agent accepted.

reach.task: Describe what is actually on offer before the client chooses.
reach.learn: A listed offer is not the sale.

evidence.claim: A record can list itinerary packages and incentives the carriers have already offered. It cannot describe or sell them.
This conversation is with a customer who has asked. It is not an outbound call, which would need its own consent rules.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A travel agent in a mid-size European company. A tariff line is not a trip, and a draft is not a booking.
Fields: A carrier id and a package id are required. An offer with no id is not listed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the travel agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The customer is already in the conversation. This task does not place an outbound sales call.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the travel agent.
unknowns: Whether promotional incentives are stored as packages or only printed in a brochure.
research_questions: Which carrier offers are still known only from a brochure and not on the package record?

already_counted.description: Planning, describing, and selling the itinerary stay with the agent.

incremental.description: Check the listed packages are ones these carriers currently offer.

approvals.approved_version: itinerary version and the package ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes offers have no package id, so the agent works from brochures. High assumes the current offers are listed. Describing and selling stay with the agent.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the open questions on destination, dates, budget, and rooms.
Converse with the customer to determine destination, transportation, dates, and accommodations.
Record the travel dates and the financial considerations they required.

tasks.design: Open questions on destination, mode, dates, budget, and rooms are shown from {CRM}. The travel agent converses with the customer to determine the destination, the transportation, the dates, the financial considerations, and the accommodations required. A question with no enquiry id is still asked by the agent. The list does not hold the conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were caught or missed depending on what the agent remembered to ask.
tasks.enabler_now: A short question list can sit beside the conversation. The agent still listens.
tasks.still_hard: What the customer can spend, and what they actually want, comes out in the talk.
tasks.human_edge: The agent determines the trip with the customer. A checklist does not.
tasks.altitude: The conversation stays with the agent. The note records only what the customer stated.

reach.task: Hear what cover the customer actually needs.
reach.learn: A question list is not the conversation.

evidence.claim: A question list can remind the agent to ask destination, dates, budget, and rooms. It cannot hold the conversation.
Financial considerations here are the customer's travel budget. They are not a credit decision and not investment advice.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A travel agent in a mid-size European company. A tariff line is not a trip, and a draft is not a booking.

Fields: An enquiry id is required before the question list is shown. The agent still converses if it is missing. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the travel agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The note records what the customer stated. It does not infer a budget they did not give.
unknowns: Whether the conversation is in the shop, on the phone, or in a written thread.
research_questions: Which trip facts are still only in the agent's memory after the conversation?

already_counted.description: The conversation and the note of what the customer stated stay with the agent.

incremental.description: Check the question list matches this enquiry, not a previous customer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes there is no enquiry id, so the agent asks from habit and nothing is saved. High assumes the questions are shown. The conversation itself is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute the cost from the tariff.

steps.what: Compute costs of travel and accommodations using carrier tariff books.

loop.purpose: Bind each cost line to a tariff or hotel rate id.
loop.input: A line and the tariff or rate book.
loop.output: The line with a rate id and the stored amount, or a gap.
loop.check: The rate id is in the book, and the amount is the amount on that rate.
loop.stop: Stop when a line has no rate id or states an amount the book does not hold.
loop.why_not_simpler: A single total cannot tell which cost line is missing from the carrier tariff or the hotel rate book.

steps.what: Quote the package tour cost on a calculator or computer.
Send the accepted quote that cites the hotel rate books.

tasks.design: Costs of travel and accommodations are computed in {DOCS} only from carrier tariff books and hotel rate books the company holds. Each line must cite a rate id. The travel agent quotes the package tour cost, on a calculator or a computer when a rate is missing, and accepts the total. {EMAIL} sends only that accepted quote. A line with no rate is not computed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fares were added on a calculator from books that were not the current edition.
tasks.enabler_now: A tariff the company holds can price a line. A line with no rate id stops.
tasks.still_hard: A package that is not in the book, and whether the total is the one to offer, is the agent's quote.
tasks.human_edge: The agent accepts the quote. A computed line is not a fare the customer has been told.
tasks.altitude: The customer sees a cost only after the agent accepts it, and every line cites a tariff or a hotel rate.

reach.role: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
reach.task: Quote a figure that is in the book.
reach.learn: A total with a missing rate is not sent.

evidence.claim: Carrier tariff lines and hotel rates the company holds can be summed. A missing rate cannot be filled in.

A cost told to a customer has to be a line in the carrier tariff, the hotel rate book, or a package the company holds. Air Canada was held liable when a chatbot stated a fare the tariff did not support.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A travel agent in a mid-size European company. A tariff line is not a trip, and a draft is not a booking.
Fields: A tariff id or a rate id is required on every cost line. A missing id stops the line. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the travel agent finishes it by hand.
Native check: The amount on a line is the amount in the book. The compute step does not invent a fare.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the travel agent.
unknowns: Whether hotel rates are in the same book as carrier tariffs or in a separate file.
research_questions: Which quotes still include a figure that is not in the current tariff?

already_counted.description: Quoting the package and accepting the total stay with the agent.

incremental.description: Read each cost line against the tariff before accepting the quote.

approvals.approved_version: quote version and the rate ids it cites

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes many lines have no rate id, so the agent prices them from the books by hand. High assumes the tariff prices the lines and the agent only accepts the total. Nothing is sent before acceptance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The travel agent still talks with the customer, still sells the trip, and still takes the payment. A cost is computed only from a tariff or a package the company holds, and the customer sees it only after the agent accepts that total.
reach: Insurance sales agents accept a quote before it is sent, and this job learns a travel cost is accepted the same way.
Securities, commodities, and financial services sales agents do not invent a price, and this job learns a fare line must cite the tariff.
skills_to_grow: Read a cost line back to the tariff or the package before quoting it.
Hear the destination, the dates, and the budget in the customer's own words.
Take payment only for an amount the customer and the agent have both seen.
role.ambitious_version: Every quoted trip cites the tariff or package it came from, and the agent still decides what to sell after hearing what the customer needs.
